**Wallue Street wrote:**

I think this bug was somehow reintroduced. I am using sqlalchemy v1.2.8 with Python v3.6.6 and with MSSQL

My model class is:

```
from datetime import date
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, Date, String, ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship

from models import dbModel


class Mapping(dbModel):

    __tablename__ = 'mappings'

    id: int = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True, name='MappingId')
    type_id: int = Column(Integer, nullable=False, name='EntityMappingTypeID')
    mapping_as_of: date = Column(Date, nullable=False, name='MappingNameAsOf')
    entity_id: int = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('RS_Entity.EntityID'), name='EntityID')
    internal_name: str = Column(String, name='InternalName')
    external_name: str = Column(String, name='ExternalName')

```

When executing the following bulk_update

```
session.bulk_update_mappings(Mapping, [{'entity_id': 8582, 'type_id': 1, 'external_name': '### Test ###', 'internal_name': None, 'mapping_as_of': Timestamp('2016-04-01 00:00:00'), 'id': 1553}])
```
Since I have SQL echo enabled I can clearly see the UPDATE statement generated is wrong, because it's trying to set the Primary Key (MappingId):

```
2018-11-01 15:13:06,780 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine BEGIN (implicit)
BEGIN (implicit)
2018-11-01 15:13:49,286 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine UPDATE dbo.[mappings] SET [MappingId]=?, [EntityMappingTypeID]=?, [MappingNameAsOf]=?, [EntityID]=?, [InternalName]=?, [ExternalName]=? WHERE dbo.[mappings].[MappingId] = ?
UPDATE dbo.[RS_EntityMapping] SET [MappingId]=?, [EntityMappingTypeID]=?, [MappingNameAsOf]=?, [EntityID]=?, [InternalName]=?, [ExternalName]=? WHERE dbo.[mappings].[MappingId] = ?
2018-11-01 15:13:49,292 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine (1553, 1, Timestamp('2016-04-01 00:00:00'), 8582, None, '### Test ###', 1553)
(1553, 1, Timestamp('2016-04-01 00:00:00'), 8582, None, '### Test ###', 1553)
2018-11-01 15:13:49,327 INFO sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine ROLLBACK
ROLLBACK
```
Stepping into the code I can see the issue is in the code: **sqlalchemy/orm/persistence.py:676**
```
stmt = table.update(clause)
```

Interestingly, if I remove the alternative name from my Primary Key, and change id to MappingId as the attribute name, it then works properly. So it all points to an issue with aliased primary keys that are autoincrement.

Please help, thank you!

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

hi there -

the update statement is apparently less than ideal but not "wrong" since it is still adding the primary key column to the WHERE clause.   the tests here aren't asserting that the SQL is correct which is why this silent failure was allowed to pass, but you'd still get the right result.   I guess because you are using SQL server you're getting an IDENTITY problem?

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

OK here is your workaround, set the key on the column also:

    id: int = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True, name='MappingId', key='id')


that's what it's looking at right now

**Wallue Street wrote:**

Great, that workaround works perfectly. Thank you!

issue.title: alt-key primary key on bulk update UPDATES the pk as well as having it in the WHERE clause
issue.body:
**Migrated issue, originally created by Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek))**

continuing from #3849:

    py.test test/orm/test_bulk.py -s --log-debug=sqlalchemy.engine -k test_update_attrs


the UPDATE statement is re-SETing the pk attribute needlessly (which can fail on SQL server):

    UPDATE people_attrs SET person_id=?, name=? WHERE people_attrs.person_id = ?
    INFO:sqlalchemy.engine.base.Engine:(5, 'newname', 5)

the tests need to assert_sql
